h1: What is the difference between a special permit and a variance in Newton?
title: Special Permits vs. Variances in Newton, MA
description: Who grants special permits and variances in Newton, the two-thirds City Council vote, site plan approval, and the legal tests for a variance.
short_answer: The City Council grants special permits, by a two-thirds vote of all councilors, together with site plan approval. Variances are heard by the Zoning Board of Appeals. A variance requires conditions such as soil, shape or topography that especially affect the property, plus substantial hardship.

facts.text: The City Council grants special permits by a two-thirds vote of all the Council (Sec. 7.3.3.A).
A special-permit application requires concurrent site plan approval (Sec. 7.3.1.A).
Findings include an appropriate site, no adverse effect on the neighborhood, and no nuisance or serious vehicle or pedestrian hazard (Sec. 7.3.3.C).
Examples include increased FAR and a third story for detached houses (Sec. 3.1.9.A.2, 3.2.11.A.2).
Variance applications are heard by the Zoning Board of Appeals (Sec. 7.6.1.A).
The property must have soil, shape or topography conditions that especially affect it, rather than the district generally (Sec. 7.6.1.B).
Literal enforcement must cause substantial hardship (Sec. 7.6.1.C).
Relief must not substantially harm the public good or undermine the ordinance's intent (Sec. 7.6.1.D).

qa.q: Who approves special permits in Newton?
qa.a: The City Council, by a two-thirds vote of all councilors (Sec. 7.3.3.A).

qa.q: Can I get a special permit to build a larger house?
qa.a: The ordinance lists increased FAR as something a special permit may allow (Sec. 3.1.9.A.2).

qa.q: What do I need to show for a variance?
qa.a: Conditions of soil, shape or topography that especially affect the property, substantial hardship, and no substantial detriment to the public good (Sec. 7.6.1).
